source: CDISC ADaM BDS for Population Pharmacokinetics Implementation Guide v1.0 (2023-10-06)

dataset_metadata.data_structure_description: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
dataset_metadata.structure: One record per subject per parameter (analyte) per analysis timepoint per event (dosing or observation)
dataset_metadata.cdisc_notes: Dataset designed to support PPK. Sourced from SDTM (e.g., PC, DM, EX, LB) and ADaM (e.g., ADSL and ADEX datasets).

variables.label: Project Identifier
variables.guidance: Text representing protocol or compound name.

variables.label: Project Identifier (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of PROJID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.guidance: STUDYID. Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

variables.label: Study Identifier (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of STUDYID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Part of the Study
variables.guidance: As defined per protocol. Required when study has more than 1 part (e.g., part A, dose escalation and part B, dose evaluation). In SDTM it is mapped in STUDYID by some sponsor companies.

variables.label: Subject Type
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of subject type.

variables.label: Subject Type (C)
variables.guidance: Unique character representation of SUBJTYP. For first-in-human studies, the value can be 'Healthy volunteers'.

variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.guidance: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of USUBJID.

variables.label: Subject Identifier for the Study
variables.guidance: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

variables.label: Subject Identifier for the Study (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of SUBJID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Study Site Identifier
variables.guidance: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

variables.label: Study Site Identifier (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of SITEID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Record Sequence
variables.guidance: Derived sequence for the whole dataset. Sequential values should start with 1 on the first non-header row and increment by 1 for each subsequent row. Often used for convenience and merging of PK and PD datasets. Can also be useful for tracking outlier exclusion.

variables.label: Actual Rel Time from First Dose
variables.guidance: Actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to study treatment. Could be negative. Derived from (ADTM of the current event/record) - (ADTM of the first dosing event/record of the subject).

variables.label: Relative Time Unit
variables.guidance: Units for all reference times AFRLT, APRLT, NFRLT, NPRLT. Add the unit here or in the time variable label.

variables.label: Actual Rel Time from Previous Dose
variables.guidance: Derived from (ADTM of the current event/record) - (ADTM of the previous dosing event/record of the subject).

variables.label: Nominal Rel Time from First Dose
variables.guidance: Planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to study treatment. For PK it will be in the PC dataset.

variables.label: Nominal Rel Time from Previous Dose
variables.guidance: For PK it can be derived from planned elapsed time from reference exposure to study treatment or equivalent variable that has nominal time in the PC dataset.

variables.label: Occasion
variables.guidance: Occasion is a grouping variable. It groups dose and concentration observations for a particular dosing. The implementation is taken directly from the specs/protocol and defined by the modeler. This is a popPK software variable.

variables.label: Record Exclusion
variables.guidance: It can be captured prior to the modeling or after some analysis, with possible iterations and adjustments. Possible reasons: BLOQ, biological implausibility, IWER > threshold, incorrect dosing information.

variables.label: Comment for the Record Exclusion
variables.guidance: It can be captured prior to the modeling or after some analysis. Possible reasons: BLOQ, biological implausibility, outlier based on variability metrics, incorrect dosing information, day 1 pre-dose sample. Can also be coded through numbers connected with different reasons.

variables.label: Identification of Data Issue Reason
variables.guidance: Captures primary reason for identifying the record for data issues (e.g., dose time imputation flags). Sequential number starting with 1, increments with each unique reason.

variables.label: Identification of Data Issue Reason (C)
variables.guidance: Character version of FLGREAS.

variables.label: Event ID
variables.guidance: EVID=1 is Dosing Event, EVID=0 is observation. It can be expanded to other numbers as defined in the dataset specs. This is a popPK software variable.

variables.label: Dependent Variable Name
variables.guidance: Analyte/drug name/other measurements (e.g., PC.PCTEST for PK, EX or ADEX for dose, ADLB for labs).

variables.label: Dependent Variable Name (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of DVID. Convention is normally 0=dose, 1=for the first observation of interest, etc. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Compartment
variables.guidance: Derived based on the specifications from modeler. This is a popPK software variable.

variables.label: Dependent Variable Result
variables.guidance: Numeric result of dependent variable applicable to observation events. DV is a widely used notation in the field of pharmacometrics since its inception for the value of dependent variable (observation). This is a copy of AVAL.

variables.label: Analysis Value
variables.guidance: Numeric analysis value described by PARAM.

variables.label: Dependent Variable Unit
variables.guidance: Unit for DV and AVAL.

variables.label: Result or Finding in Standard Format
variables.guidance: Character results/findings of dependent variable in a standard format. Purpose is to capture which records are BLQ or ALQ in the DV column. U is a replacement for the dataset name (e.g., USTRESC equals PCSTRESC for PC records).

variables.label: Missing Dependent Variable Result
variables.guidance: If DV=. then MDV=1. When DV is missing for observation then MDV=1, when EVID=1 then MDV=1. Controlled terms: 0, 1. This is a popPK software variable.

variables.label: Analysis Upper Limit of Quantitation
variables.guidance: In assay report.

variables.label: Analysis Lower Limit of Quantitation
variables.guidance: LLOQ of PK, PD and any other sources.

variables.label: Below Lower Limit of Quant Flag
variables.guidance: N, Y. Set to Y when the analysis value is below the limit of quantification. Controlled terms: N, Y.

variables.label: Below Lower Limit of Quant Flag (N)
variables.guidance: 0=N, 1=Y. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable. Controlled terms: 0, 1.

variables.label: Above the Upper Limit of Quant Flag
variables.guidance: N, Y. Set to Y when the analysis value is above the limit of quantification. Controlled terms: N, Y.

variables.label: Above the Upper Limit of Quant Flag (N)
variables.guidance: 0=N, 1=Y. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable. Controlled terms: 0, 1.

variables.label: Actual Amount of Dose Received (unit)
variables.guidance: Only populated on dosing records.

variables.label: Actual Treatment Dose (unit)
variables.guidance: DOSEA represents the actual treatment dosage associated with the record. Could be amount (mg) or weight based dose (mg/kg). Units of AMT and DOSEA can be same or different. This is the actual numeric amount of the dose used for the population analysis and may differ from the EX.EXDOSE. Populated on all individual records as carry-forward.

variables.label: Total Daily Amt of Dose Received (unit)
variables.guidance: Used mostly for BID dosing schemes.

variables.label: Duration Of Dose Administration (unit)
variables.guidance: Duration associated with infusion (IV, SC); distinct from TRTDURD, TRTDURM, and TRTDURY, which reference the duration of the entire study rather than the duration of a single treatment event. Derived from EXENDTC - EXSTDTC. The label should contain the unit of time. Usually same unit as time variables.

variables.label: Infusion Rate (unit)
variables.guidance: Calculated as the amount of dose received divided by the dose duration. Certain modeling methods may require that RATE is set to a specific value. The label should contain the unit (e.g., mg/hr).

variables.label: Dosing Interval (unit)
variables.guidance: Describes the dosing frequency for multiple doses (e.g., 24 for QD, 12 for BID, if time unit is hours).

variables.label: Number Of Additional Doses
variables.guidance: Number of additional doses like the current dosing event until the next captured dose. Commonly used for long-lasting studies with frequent dosing to keep the dataset manageable.

variables.label: Steady State
variables.guidance: A steady-state dose is a dose presumed to be the last of a series of implied doses, each exactly like the dose in question, given at a regular interval specified by II and leading to steady state by the time the steady-state dose is given.

variables.label: Drug Formulation
variables.guidance: Type of formulation (e.g., tablet, capsule, aerosol); EX.EXDOSFRM or protocol. Codelist: FRM.

variables.label: Drug Formulation (N)
variables.guidance: Unique numerical representation of FORM. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from the corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Route of Administration
variables.guidance: Route of treatment delivery. May be derived from EX.EXROUTE. Codelist: ROUTE.

variables.label: Route of Administration (N)
variables.guidance: Derived from ROUTE as one-on-one unique match. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

variables.label: Analysis Cycle
variables.guidance: Record-level identifier that reflects cycle and may be of particular importance for studies that examine concentrations in cancer patients from AVISIT or protocol.

variables.label: Analysis Cycle (C)
variables.guidance: Derived from ACYCLE as one-on-one unique match. The character versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding numeric pair variable.

variables.label: Cohort Subject Enrolled Into
variables.guidance: Subject-level variable. Could be some sort of subpopulation.

variables.label: Cohort Subject Enrolled into (C)
variables.guidance: Character representation of the COHORT variable. There must be a one-to-one mapping to COHORT.

variables.label: Date and Time of the Event
variables.guidance: Datetime associated with event ID represented in ISO 8601 character format. U is a replacement for the dataset name from where the value came from (e.g., UDTC equals PCDTC for PC records).

variables.label: Body Weight (unit)
variables.guidance: Variable may be derived from VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets. Weight is associated with sampling time. SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset.

variables.label: Baseline Body Weight (unit)
variables.guidance: Weight associated with the last assessment prior to dosing. Use flags for baseline. If the definition matches the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

variables.label: Baseline Body Height (unit)
variables.guidance: Variable may be derived from baseline VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN. If the definition matches the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

variables.label: Baseline Body Mass Index (unit)
variables.guidance: May be derived from baseline VS or other datasets. ADSL.BMIBL for baseline and VS.BMI for time-varying or derived. If the definition matches the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

variables.label: Body Surface Area at Baseline (unit)
variables.guidance: May be derived from baseline VS or other datasets. ADSL.BSABL for baseline and VS.BSA for time-varying or derived. If the definition matches the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

variables.label: Age
variables.guidance: DM.AGE or ADSL.AGE. If analysis needs require a derived age that does not match ADSL.AGE, then AAGE (Analysis Age) must be added.

variables.label: Age at Analysis Timepoint (unit)
variables.guidance: Number of years between BRTHDT and ADT.

variables.label: Sex
variables.guidance: The sex of the subject is a required variable in ADSL; must be identical to ADSL.SEX. Codelist: SEX.

variables.label: Sex (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of SEX. Can be extended to other values beyond 1 and 2. Example values: 1=M, 2=F.

variables.label: Race
variables.guidance: The race of the subject is a required variable in ADSL; identical to ADSL.RACE. May categorize differently if analysis demands. Codelist: RACE.

variables.label: Race (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of RACE. Example: 1=American Indian or Alaska Native, 2=Asian, 3=Black/African American, 4=Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, 5=White. If races need to be categorized differently, use ARACE and ARACEN.

variables.label: Analysis Race
variables.guidance: To allow different definitions of race. For example, coding American Indian/Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander as 'Other'. Analysis-specific and could vary based on analysis needs.

variables.label: Analysis Race (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of ARACE. Example: 1=White, 2=Black/African American, 3=Asian, 4=Other, 5=Unknown.

variables.label: Analysis Ethnicity
variables.guidance: Ethnicity as needed for analysis. May be derived.

variables.label: Analysis Ethnicity (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of AETHNIC.

variables.label: Geographic Region y
variables.guidance: REGIONy is a permissible variable in ADSL.

variables.label: Geographic Region y (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of REGIONy.

variables.label: Country
variables.guidance: DM.COUNTRY or ADSL.COUNTRY.

variables.label: Country Full Name
variables.guidance: COUNTRYL is a human-readable name of the DM.COUNTRY value.

variables.label: Country (N)
variables.guidance: Numeric version of COUNTRY.

variables.label: Baseline Creatinine Serum (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for creatinine serum per the algorithm defined in the SAP.

variables.label: Baseline Creatinine Clearance (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for creatinine clearance per the algorithm defined in the SAP. A formula may be suggested if the value does not exist in the lab dataset.

variables.label: Baseline eGFR (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for eGFR per the algorithm defined in the SAP. A formula may be suggested if the value does not exist in the lab dataset.

variables.label: Baseline Total Bilirubin (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for total bilirubin per the algorithm defined in the SAP.

variables.label: Baseline Aspartate transaminase (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for aspartate transaminase per the algorithm defined in the SAP.

variables.label: Baseline Alanine transaminase (unit)
variables.guidance: Use the baseline lab value for alanine transaminase per the algorithm defined in the SAP.

conformance_rules.description: ADPPK has one record per subject per parameter (analyte) per analysis timepoint per event (dosing or observation).
Required variables (Core=Req): STUDYID, USUBJID, USUBJIDN, AFRLT, EVID, DV, MDV, AMT, SEX, RACE.
STUDYID must be identical to the ADSL variable.
USUBJID must be identical to the ADSL variable.
SUBJID must be identical to the ADSL variable.
SITEID must be identical to the ADSL variable.
SEX must be identical to ADSL.SEX.
RACE must be identical to ADSL.RACE (may categorize differently if analysis demands).

If both a character variable and its numeric counterpart are present and both populated on a row, there must be a one-to-one mapping between the 2 variables on all rows within the scope on which both variables are populated.
EVID=1 for dosing events, EVID=0 for observations.
MDV=1 when DV is missing for observation or when EVID=1. Controlled terms: 0, 1.
DV is a copy of AVAL.
AMT is only populated on dosing records.
BLQFL set to Y when the analysis value is below the limit of quantification. Controlled terms: N, Y.
ALQFL set to Y when the analysis value is above the limit of quantification. Controlled terms: N, Y.
PART is required when study has more than 1 part (e.g., part A dose escalation and part B dose evaluation).
COHORTC must have a one-to-one mapping to COHORT.
ROUTEN is derived from ROUTE as one-on-one unique match.
ACYCLEC is derived from ACYCLE as one-on-one unique match.
AFRLT is derived from (ADTM of the current event/record) - (ADTM of the first dosing event/record of the subject). Could be negative.
APRLT is derived from (ADTM of the current event/record) - (ADTM of the previous dosing event/record of the subject).
If SDTM character variables are converted to numeric variables, they should be named as they are in the SDTM with an 'N' suffix added.
Dataset should use ADPPK as a prefix (recommended, not required). Other relevant information can be used in the dataset name (e.g., ADPPKxyz).
ADPPK is of Class BASIC DATA STRUCTURE, SubClass POPULATION PHARMACOKINETIC ANALYSIS.
Dataset keys are USUBJID, AFRLT (Actual Rel Time from First Dose), DVID, EVID (Event ID).

Covariates follow suffix conventions: <COV> for time-varying, <COV>BL for baseline, <COV>N for numeric version of categorical covariate (one-to-one with <COV>), <COV>I for imputed values, <COV>GRy for grouping covariates.
RATE is calculated as AMT/DOSEDUR.
Variable units should be specified in the variable label.
DOSEDUR and RATE labels should contain the unit of time or unit.
Missing values may be specifically coded depending on the tool (e.g., -99), which would be described as a nonvalid value in the metadata.
Handling of missing values must be clearly documented in the dataset specifications, SAP, or PAP.
Imputed date/time records, imputed clock-time records, and imputed amount records should be flagged.
When identifying the source dataset for a variable, the immediate predecessor variable is used per ADaM v2.1.
All data sources used are to be indicated and provided as supporting information.
ADT and related variables represent start date and time for dosing or interval sample collection; AENDT and related variables represent end date and time.
If analysis needs require a derived age that does not match ADSL.AGE, then AAGE (Analysis Age) must be added.
